job_description: Job Context: The Centre for Disability in Development (CDD) is a non-profit organization established in 1996 to develop a more inclusive society for persons with disabilities. CDD simultaneously builds technical capacities of the development stakeholders and the communities in how to be more inclusive whilst also enabling persons with a disability to participate in society by strengthening their leadership and providing them with essential rehabilitation and other supports. CDD is one of the most renowned organizations in the field of disability-inclusive development. CDD’s work in Bangladesh is supported by international and national donor agencies/development partners. CDD offers an inclusive, amicable, and respectable work environment. The Ramon Magsaysay Award (Asian version of the Noble prize) has been awarded to its former Executive Director in 2010. In 2018, CDD was recognized by the Government of Bangladesh as one of the best organizations working on disability and development issues. CDD is implementing multiple humanitarian and development projects at Ukhiya and Teknaf in Cox's Bazar and BhasanChar with the support of Handicap International (HI), Humanity & Inclusion. Maintain a sound understanding of volunteer recruitment procedures at the Rohingya camp level. Coordinate volunteer recruitment with the respective CiC offices and ensure compliance with relevant RRRC and ISCG guidelines. Ensure that newly recruited staff receive and sign their employment contracts in a timely manner and that all relevant joining documents are completed and forwarded to the concerned departments or offices. Ensure that individual personnel files are opened for all new employees, regularly updated using a standard checklist, and maintained in an organized and systematic manner. Ensure the integrity, security, and confidentiality of all staff-related data and personnel records. Maintain an effective filing and documentation system for all HR-related records and provide relevant information to managers and staff as required, in line with confidentiality requirements. Ensure that all newly recruited staff receive appropriate orientation and induction on organizational policies, procedures, roles, and responsibilities. Maintain and regularly update the HR directory, ensuring that all necessary staff information is accurate and up to date. Performance Appraisal: Provide support in developing, reviewing, and updating job descriptions in consultation with the respective line managers. Support the development of staff skills, competencies, and professional capabilities through appropriate learning and development initiatives. Monitor employee performance and coordinate with relevant staff to ensure that performance evaluations are conducted within the specified timelines and the results are communicated to the respective employees. Compensation, Benefits Management: Ensure the timely and accurate preparation of monthly payroll, including verification of working days, applicable benefits, and other relevant entitlements. Ensure proper tracking and management of staff leave, attendance, movement, and absences, and maintain appropriate supporting documentation. Monitor and maintain volunteer attendance records, prepare volunteer payment sheets in a timely manner, and submit them to the Finance Department for processing within the stipulated timeframe. Review compensation and benefits packages periodically in collaboration with the Accounts and Management Team. Support annual salary scale assessments to ensure that CDD's salary structure and compensation packages remain fair, consistent, and competitive. Employee Relations: Ensure the timely processing and documentation of new employment contracts, contract extensions, staff transfers, promotions, and other changes in employment status. Manage and coordinate processes related to disciplinary actions, staff separation, and employment termination in accordance with organizational policies and procedures. Respond promptly and effectively to all HR-related queries and requests from employees. Ensure that employee personnel files and HR records are properly maintained, up to date, and readily available for real-time audits in compliance with organizational policies and relevant donor requirements. Training & Development: Coordinate and facilitate staff training and professional development initiatives to enhance employees' knowledge, skills, and competencies. Support the planning and implementation of team-building activities and initiatives to promote teamwork, collaboration, and a positive working environment. Develop and implement a staff training and development plan in coordination with the Management and Finance Teams, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and available resources. Administrative and Procurement work: Coordinate administrative and logistical support, including fleet management and transport arrangements, for project offices and field teams in Ukhiya, Teknaf, and Cox’s Bazar. Arrange hotel accommodation, training venues, and vehicle reservations for national and international staff and consultants. Ensure timely issuance and replacement of staff ID cards. Prepare and submit administrative reports and statistics as required. Maintain office health, safety, hygiene, and security standards. Ensure timely payment of utility bills and other office-related expenses. Ensure smooth office operations through proper maintenance and management of facilities, supplies, equipment, and vehicles. Supervise support staff and ensure regular office cleaning and maintenance. Ensure timely processing of purchase requisitions, requests for quotations (RFQs), and purchase orders in accordance with CDD policies and procedures. Prepare, review, and update lease and service contracts, ensuring compliance with organizational and statutory requirements. Lead and coordinate procurement activities in compliance with CDD's procurement policies and procedures. Conduct periodic physical verification of project assets and maintain an updated asset inventory. Maintain proper records of asset handover and takeover during staff joining, transfer, and separation. Ensure all assets are properly tagged with unique serial numbers and that the inventory records are regularly updated. Perform any other relevant duties assigned by the authorized supervisor. Safeguarding Responsibilities: Adhere to CDD's Children and Adults at Risk Safeguarding policy, ensuring the safety and well-being of all project participants. Promote a safe and secure environment for all participants and stakeholders of the project. Report any safeguarding concerns promptly and follow the designated reporting procedures. Additional Responsibilities: Perform any other responsibility/ special duty delegated by project and CDD management.

Complete technical closure after buyer approval by issuing signed documents to all stakeholders and ensuring bulk production strictly follows approved standards. Review pre-production documents and complete fabric risk assessments in collaboration with Merchandising, Factory, and Quality teams before production. Participate in risk assessment meetings for high-risk orders and implement appropriate mitigation plans to minimize production risks. Review and approve subsequent bulk fabric submissions by ensuring consistency with approved first bulk standards and established colour tolerances. Coordinate with the ZXY Laboratory to validate factory assessments and ensure accurate comments are issued for colour and testing results. Monitor weekly and monthly laboratory performance trends to evaluate supplier quality and identify opportunities for improvement. Lead continuous quality improvement initiatives by analyzing laboratory findings, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions. Collaborate with the laboratory and suppliers to resolve recurring quality issues and improve overall fabric production performance. Conduct formal technical evaluations of fabric mills using the approved Mill Evaluation Form before placing production orders. Obtain all required management approvals for mill evaluations before confirming orders and proceeding with production

The Senior Rehabilitation Officer will supervise rehabilitation personnel, strengthen clinical practices, promote disability inclusion, and coordinate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams and relevant stakeholders to improve patients’ functional independence, quality of life, and community reintegration. The role will also support program development, staff capacity building, data management, quality assurance, and compliance with PHD policies, relevant Ministry of Health requirements, safeguarding standards, and humanitarian principles. Key Responsibilities A. Clinical Rehabilitation Services and Technical Leadership Lead and oversee the delivery of rehabilitation services to patients with musculoskeletal conditions, neurological disorders, physical disabilities, injuries, burns, fractures, post-operative conditions, and other rehabilitation needs. Conduct or supervise comprehensive functional assessments to identify patients’ rehabilitation needs, functional limitations, and individualized treatment goals. Develop, review, and monitor individualized rehabilitation plans based on clinical findings, patient priorities, and evidence-based practices. Provide and supervise appropriate rehabilitation interventions, including therapeutic exercises, strengthening, balance and gait training, mobility training, positioning, functional rehabilitation, and pain management techniques within professional scope of practice. Assess patients’ needs for assistive devices and mobility aids and facilitate appropriate prescription, fitting, training, and referral within professional authorization and available resources. Monitor patient progress, evaluate treatment outcomes, and modify rehabilitation plans based on clinical improvement and functional goals. Ensure timely identification and referral of patients requiring specialized rehabilitation, medical evaluation, or multidisciplinary intervention. Promote safe patient handling, prevention of secondary complications, and continuity of rehabilitation care. Provide technical guidance on complex cases and support rehabilitation staff in clinical decision-making within their professional scope of practice. Ensure clinical records, assessments, treatment plans, and follow-up documentation meet established standards. B. Clinical Supervision and Quality Assurance Supervise and provide technical guidance to Rehabilitation Officers, Rehabilitation Assistants, and other assigned rehabilitation personnel. Conduct regular case reviews, clinical discussions, and supportive supervision sessions to strengthen service quality. Monitor staff compliance with approved clinical protocols, professional standards, IPC measures, patient safety procedures, and organizational guidelines. Identify gaps in rehabilitation service delivery and implement corrective actions in coordination with the supervisor. Promote evidence-based practice, ethical conduct, informed consent, patient dignity, confidentiality, and patient-centered care. Monitor patient feedback and complaints related to rehabilitation services and support appropriate resolution through established mechanisms. Support clinical audits, service quality assessments, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. Ensure appropriate use, maintenance, and accountability of rehabilitation equipment, assistive devices, and other program resources. C. Program Planning, Implementation, and Coordination Support the planning, implementation, and monitoring of rehabilitation activities in accordance with project objectives, work plans, and organizational priorities. Develop and review rehabilitation activity plans, service schedules, patient follow-up plans, and other operational requirements. Coordinate with Medical Officers, Nurses, Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists where available, Nutrition, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Community Health teams, and other relevant departments to ensure integrated patient care. Participate in multidisciplinary case conferences and contribute to comprehensive care planning for patients with complex rehabilitation needs. Strengthen referral and counter-referral systems between healthcare facilities, community-based services, and specialized rehabilitation providers. Support community-based rehabilitation, post-discharge follow-up, and continuity of care for patients with disabilities and long-term rehabilitation needs. Promote disability inclusion, accessibility, and equitable access to healthcare services for people with disabilities. Coordinate with relevant government authorities, humanitarian partners, NGOs/INGOs, and service providers as required. Support the development and implementation of standard operating procedures, technical guidelines, and service delivery tools relevant to rehabilitation activities. D. Staff Management and Capacity Building Provide day-to-day technical supervision and guidance to assigned rehabilitation personnel. Allocate duties, monitor staff performance, and ensure effective use of available human resources in coordination with the supervisor. Identify staff training needs and develop or support appropriate capacity-building plans. Conduct orientation, on-the-job training, and mentoring on functional assessment, rehabilitation planning, therapeutic interventions, safe patient handling, positioning, mobility assistance, disability inclusion, and prevention of secondary complications. Provide basic rehabilitation orientation to relevant healthcare workers, community health workers, and community volunteers within their respective roles. Promote teamwork, accountability, respectful communication, and a supportive learning environment. Contribute to staff performance reviews, professional development, and competency assessments as assigned. Ensure staff understand and comply with organizational policies, safeguarding requirements, professional ethics, and applicable clinical procedures. E. Data Management, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting Ensure accurate and timely documentation of patient registrations, functional assessments, rehabilitation plans, treatment sessions, referrals, and follow-up outcomes. Oversee the collection, compilation, verification, and analysis of rehabilitation service data. Monitor key service indicators, patient outcomes, service utilization, referral completion, and progress against project targets. Prepare and submit weekly, monthly, quarterly, and other required narrative and statistical reports. Identify service delivery gaps, operational challenges, and trends in rehabilitation needs and recommend evidence-based improvements. Support monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) activities, assessments, and data quality reviews. Maintain patient confidentiality and ensure secure handling, storage, and sharing of health information in accordance with organizational policies. Contribute to project reviews, donor reporting, work-plan development, and other program documentation as required. F. Patient, Caregiver, and Community Engagement Educate patients and caregivers on home exercise programs, safe positioning, mobility, activities of daily living (ADLs), injury prevention, and prevention of secondary complications. Promote adherence to rehabilitation plans and encourage active participation in recovery and functional improvement. Support awareness sessions on disability prevention, early identification of rehabilitation needs, assistive devices, and available rehabilitation services. Promote respectful, inclusive, and non-discriminatory care for people with disabilities, older people, children, and other vulnerable groups. Apply culturally sensitive communication approaches when engaging with Rohingya refugees and host communities. Incorporate patient and caregiver feedback into rehabilitation planning and service improvement. Support appropriate follow-up and community reintegration for patients requiring ongoing rehabilitation support. G. Safeguarding, IPC, and Risk Management Ensure compliance with PHD’s Code of Conduct, Child Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) requirements, anti-harassment standards, and other applicable safeguarding policies. Ensure patients are treated with dignity and respect and that informed consent is obtained before assessments and interventions, as appropriate. Identify and report safeguarding concerns, suspected abuse, exploitation, harassment, and serious misconduct through established reporting mechanisms. Ensure rehabilitation staff follow applicable IPC guidelines, hand hygiene requirements, cleaning procedures, PPE requirements, and safe equipment-handling practices. Identify and mitigate clinical, operational, occupational health, and patient safety risks associated with rehabilitation service delivery. Ensure appropriate incident reporting and follow-up in accordance with organizational procedures. Maintain compliance with security protocols, emergency procedures, and relevant hospital or facility standards. H. Emergency Preparedness and Other Responsibilities Support the continuity and adaptation of rehabilitation services during humanitarian emergencies, disease outbreaks, natural disasters, and other disruptions. Participate in internal meetings, technical working groups, coordination forums, trainings, and program reviews. Maintain effective communication with supervisors, colleagues, partners, and relevant stakeholders. job_description: Job Description: OT Nurse - Jointly operated by Save the Children & PHD Mother and Child Hospital (MCH). Duty Station: Camp 21, Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar Position Summary The OT Nurse is responsible for providing safe, competent, and evidence-based nursing care to patients undergoing surgical and obstetric procedures at the Maternal & Child Hospital (MCH), Teknaf. The position holder supports the preparation and maintenance of the operation theatre, ensures the availability and sterility of surgical instruments and equipment, assists the surgical team during procedures, and provides appropriate pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative nursing care. The OT Nurse will ensure strict adherence to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, surgical safety protocols, patient identification procedures, safe instrument handling, and accurate clinical documentation. The role holder will work closely with surgeons, obstetricians, anaesthesia personnel, medical officers, recovery nurses, and other multidisciplinary team members to promote patient safety, quality of care, and effective surgical services in accordance with organizational policies, applicable Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) standards, and humanitarian principles. Duty Station The primary duty station is the MCH Operation Theatre. The position holder may be assigned to the recovery area, emergency procedures, or other relevant clinical areas when required and authorized, in accordance with competency and staffing requirements. Professional Scope of Practice Practise within the scope of valid Bangladesh Nursing and Midwifery Council (BNMC) registration, approved MCH protocols, and documented competencies. Administer medicines and fluids only against valid medical orders or approved protocols and within professional authorization. Perform nursing procedures only when trained, competent, and authorized. Immediately report patient deterioration, clinical incidents, equipment failures, and breaches of infection prevention or patient safety protocols. Maintain patient confidentiality, dignity, informed consent requirements, and professional boundaries at all times. 3. Key Responsibilities A. Pre-operative Nursing Care and OT Preparation Prepare the operation theatre before scheduled and emergency surgical procedures. Check the cleanliness, readiness, and functionality of OT equipment, surgical instruments, sterile supplies, suction apparatus, operating lights, and other essential equipment. Verify the availability of required surgical consumables, sterile packs, sutures, dressings, and emergency supplies before procedures. Review the operating list and coordinate with the OT In-Charge and relevant clinical teams regarding patient preparation and theatre readiness. Verify patient identity using approved identifiers and confirm the planned procedure, surgical site, relevant documentation, and consent status in coordination with the responsible clinical team. Assist with pre-operative patient assessment, preparation, positioning, skin preparation, and transfer according to approved protocols and professional scope. Confirm that required laboratory reports, clinical records, investigations, and blood products, where indicated, are available or appropriately coordinated. Ensure that the surgical safety checklist is completed at the appropriate stages in coordination with the surgical and anaesthesia teams. Maintain patient privacy, dignity, reassurance, and confidentiality throughout pre-operative preparation. B. Intra-operative Nursing Care Assist the surgical team during obstetric, gynaecological, general surgical, and other procedures performed within the hospital's approved service capacity. Perform scrub nurse and circulating nurse responsibilities according to assigned duties, training, and competency. Maintain aseptic technique and sterile fields throughout surgical procedures. Prepare, arrange, handle, and pass surgical instruments and supplies safely and efficiently. Monitor the availability of required consumables and promptly communicate any shortages to the OT In-Charge. Conduct and document surgical instrument, needle, and swab counts in collaboration with the surgical team, following approved protocols. Maintain accurate records of instruments, specimens, implants, and other relevant items where applicable. Support safe patient positioning and take appropriate measures to prevent pressure injuries, nerve injuries, and other positioning-related complications. Assist the clinical team in maintaining patient safety during procedures and promptly report any changes in patient condition or safety concerns. Label, handle, document, and transfer surgical specimens correctly according to approved procedures. Maintain clear communication with surgeons, anaesthesia personnel, and other members of the OT team. Ensure that the surgical safety checklist is completed and documented at sign-in, time-out, and sign-out, as applicable. C. Post-operative and Recovery Support Assist with safe transfer of patients from the operation theatre to the recovery area or designated clinical unit. Provide post-operative nursing care within the assigned role and competencies. Monitor and document vital signs, level of consciousness, pain, bleeding, wound condition, and other relevant observations according to clinical instructions and protocols. Recognize early signs of deterioration, including respiratory compromise, excessive bleeding, shock, and other post-operative complications, and escalate immediately to the responsible clinician. Administer prescribed medicines, fluids, and other treatments within authorized nursing responsibilities. Ensure appropriate wound dressing, drain management, and documentation according to clinical instructions and approved procedures. Provide structured verbal and written handover to the receiving nurse or clinical team. Support patient and caregiver education on post-operative care, wound care, prescribed medication, warning signs, and follow-up requirements, as appropriate. D. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Strictly comply with MCH IPC guidelines, standard precautions, and approved surgical asepsis procedures. Perform hand hygiene according to WHO's Five Moments and applicable clinical protocols. Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) during all relevant activities. Ensure proper cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization of surgical instruments and reusable equipment through approved processes. Follow established procedures for decontamination, instrument transport, sterilization, and storage in coordination with the Central Sterile Services Department (CSSD) or designated sterilization team. Maintain appropriate separation of clean, sterile, contaminated, and used equipment. Ensure safe handling and disposal of sharps, infectious waste, and other clinical waste. Never recap used needles and immediately report sharps injuries or occupational exposures for assessment and follow-up. Monitor OT environmental cleanliness and report any IPC breach, contamination, or infection risk promptly. Participate in IPC monitoring, audits, training, and corrective actions as required. E. Surgical Safety and Emergency Preparedness Ensure compliance with the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist and applicable MCH patient safety protocols. Confirm patient identification, procedure details, consent documentation, and relevant safety checks before surgery in coordination with the clinical team. Check the availability and readiness of emergency equipment, including resuscitation equipment, suction, oxygen, and other designated emergency supplies. Immediately report equipment malfunction, shortage of essential supplies, or unsafe theatre conditions. Support emergency obstetric and surgical procedures as assigned, maintaining readiness and safe workflow. Recognize and promptly escalate signs of patient deterioration, unexpected bleeding, suspected anaesthetic complications, or other emergencies. Participate in emergency drills, resuscitation training, and patient safety activities as required. Follow incident reporting procedures for adverse events, near misses, medication errors, and other patient safety concerns. F. Equipment, Instruments, and Supplies Management Maintain accountability for surgical instruments, equipment, consumables, and other OT resources. Check the condition, completeness, cleanliness, and functionality of instruments and equipment before and after procedures. Ensure proper storage and handling of sterile packs and supplies, including checks for package integrity and expiry dates. Maintain records of instrument counts, equipment checks, consumable use, and other assigned inventory documentation. Report damaged, missing, expired, or malfunctioning instruments and equipment to the OT In-Charge. Support stock monitoring and timely replenishment of essential surgical supplies. Ensure appropriate and authorized use of OT equipment and consumables. Coordinate with the Admin & Logistics, Biomedical, Pharmacy, and CSSD teams, as applicable, for maintenance, supplies, and sterilization requirements. G. Documentation, Handover, and Reporting Maintain accurate and timely nursing documentation for pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative care. Complete assigned OT registers, surgical safety checklists, instrument count records, specimen records, and other required forms. Record relevant patient observations, nursing interventions, medication administration, and clinical incidents. Provide structured handover during shift changes and patient transfers. Report OT activities, emergency procedures, supply shortages, equipment problems, and incidents to the OT In-Charge as required. Maintain confidentiality and secure handling of patient information and clinical records. Support clinical audits, data quality reviews, and quality improvement activities. H. Teamwork, Coordination, and Capacity Building Coordinate effectively with surgeons, obstetricians, anaesthesia personnel, medical officers, nurses, recovery staff, and other relevant departments. Support smooth communication and workflow between the OT, labour room, emergency department, maternity ward, inpatient units, and other clinical services. Provide practical guidance to junior nurses and assigned support personnel on OT preparation, aseptic technique, safe instrument handling, and patient safety within the scope of competence. Participate in orientation, training, clinical meetings, and professional development activities. Promote teamwork, accountability, respectful communication, and a patient-centered approach. Support service continuity during staff shortages, emergencies, and other operational challenges, as authorized. 4. Safeguarding and Accountability The position holder must comply with PHD's Code of Conduct, Save the Children's safeguarding policies, Child Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) requirements, anti-harassment standards, and applicable organizational procedures. Treat all patients and caregivers with dignity, respect, and without discrimination. Protect patient privacy and maintain confidentiality of medical and personal information. Obtain or verify informed consent in accordance with clinical protocols and applicable requirements, ensuring that the responsible clinician addresses consent for surgery and anaesthesia. Report safeguarding concerns, suspected abuse, exploitation, harassment, or serious misconduct through established reporting mechanisms. Maintain accountability for clinical decisions and nursing actions within professional scope. Follow established patient complaint, incident reporting, and accountability mechanisms. 5. General Responsibilities Comply with PHD policies, MCH hospital procedures, applicable professional standards, and relevant MoHFW guidelines. Maintain professional conduct, punctuality, confidentiality, and accountability. Follow the approved duty roster, shift handover procedures, attendance requirements, and security protocols. Protect organizational assets, surgical equipment, supplies, and infrastructure. Participate in mandatory training, clinical reviews, and quality improvement activities. Support emergency response activities and service continuity when required. Perform other relevant duties assigned by the supervisor that are consistent with the purpose of the position.

job_description: Job Description: SCANU Nurse - Jointly operated by Save the Children & PHD Mother and Child Hospital (MCH). Duty Station: Camp 21, Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar Position Summary In 2024, Save the Children Bangladesh opened a Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CEmONC) hospital (MCH) in Teknaf to meet unmet needs in maternal and neonatal emergencies. The hospital provides specialist maternal, newborn and child health care, including inpatient care, emergency obstetric and surgical care, and emergency and outpatient services, complementing existing primary health care. The SCANU Nurse provides safe, competent and evidence-based specialized nursing care to sick and small newborns admitted to the Special Care Newborn Unit (SCANU), in line with SCI, WHO and MoHFW neonatal protocols. The role holder is responsible for continuous monitoring, early recognition and escalation of deterioration, safe medication administration, infection prevention and control, family-centred care (including Kangaroo Mother Care and breastfeeding support), and safe referral of newborns who need a higher level of care. SCOPE OF ROLE: Reporting lines and accountability Line manager (direct): SCANU In-charge Nurse. Technical supervisor: Senior Medical Officer- SCANU Overall clinical oversight: Consultant Neonatologist- SCANU Staff reporting to this post: The role holder gives on-shift guidance to hygiene volunteers assigned to SCANU and attendants, without line management responsibility. Duty station SCANU is the primary duty station. The role holder is rostered in SCANU on all shifts unless temporarily deployed as described below. Cross-unit deployment (newborn care only) The role holder may be called to, or temporarily deployed in, the following areas, limited to newborn care: Labour room and obstetric OT: attend high-risk deliveries and caesarean sections when called, provide immediate newborn care and resuscitation, and transfer the newborn to SCANU when indicated. Emergency Department: triage, stabilisation and admission of sick newborns presenting to the hospital. Maternity / postnatal ward: newborn assessment, KMC follow-up and breastfeeding support for babies rooming-in with their mothers, when requested by the treating doctor. Surge or outbreak response: only when formally authorised by the SCANU In-charge Nurse and the Clinical Lead, after orientation, recorded on the duty roster, and within the role holder's competence. Before leaving SCANU, the nurse informs the in-charge and hands over his/her patients. Cross-unit deployment must not reduce SCANU below the minimum safe nurse-to-newborn staffing level agreed for the unit. Professional scope of practice Practises within the scope of BNMC registration, SCANU clinical protocols and the competencies signed off by the SCANU In-charge Nurse. Administers medicines and fluids only on a valid written medical order, or under an approved SCANU standing order or emergency protocol (e.g., neonatal resuscitation, management of hypoglycaemia), countersigned by the doctor as soon as possible. Does not prescribe, change doses or perform procedures outside signed-off competence, and seeks supervision when unsure. Does not delegate clinical tasks, medication handling or sharps handling to hygiene volunteers, attendants or caregivers. Key Responsibilities KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY: Specialised neonatal nursing care Admit newborns to SCANU: confirm identity (ID bands), and record weight, temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO2 and blood glucose, completing the admission assessment within one hour. Provide thermal care (radiant warmer, incubator, KMC), and prevent and manage hypothermia and hyperthermia. Monitor vital signs, SpO2, blood glucose, intake/output and weight at the ordered frequency, using the SCANU monitoring chart and neonatal early warning tool. Provide respiratory support (oxygen therapy and bubble CPAP as ordered), including set-up, monitoring, nasal care and weaning in collaboration with the doctor. Support feeding: breastfeeding, expressed breast milk, cup/paladai feeding and nasogastric/orogastric tube feeding, with accurate feed and fluid volumes calculated by weight and day of life. Insert and maintain peripheral IV cannulas, and run IV fluids through infusion pumps or syringe drivers, checking the site and rate at least hourly. Provide phototherapy as ordered, including eye protection, positioning, hydration and monitoring. Provide nursing care for neonatal sepsis, hypoglycaemia, birth asphyxia, prematurity and low birth weight as per protocol, and assist doctors with procedures (e.g., lumbar puncture, umbilical catheterisation, exchange transfusion). Collect, label and send laboratory samples as ordered, and follow up results. Provide cord, eye, skin and developmentally supportive care, minimising pain and unnecessary handling. Emergency recognition and escalation Recognise neonatal danger signs and deterioration (e.g., apnoea, low SpO2, bradycardia, severe hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, convulsions, poor perfusion, increasing respiratory distress) using the neonatal early warning tool. Start life-saving measures immediately (airway, bag-and-mask ventilation, chest compressions, oxygen, glucose per protocol) following neonatal resuscitation guidelines (HBB/NRP), and call for help at once. Escalate to the doctor on duty immediately for emergencies, and within the timeframe set in the SCANU escalation protocol for other early warning triggers. If there is no timely response, escalate to the Neonatologist/SMO and the SCANU In-charge Nurse. Use SBAR when communicating with doctors, and document the time of escalation, the response and the actions taken. Check the resuscitation trolley, bag-valve-masks, suction, oxygen supply and emergency medicines at the start of every shift, and restock immediately after use. Take part in neonatal resuscitation drills and mock codes. Medication safety Prepare and administer medicines following the rights of medication administration (right newborn, medicine, dose, route, time and documentation), using the newborn's current weight and the SCANU neonatal dosing and dilution guide. Carry out an independent double-check with a second nurse for high-alert medicines, dose calculations and infusion rates (e.g., aminoglycosides, phenobarbitone, caffeine/aminophylline, inotropes, concentrated dextrose and electrolytes). Label every prepared syringe and infusion; never leave medicines unlabelled or pre-drawn. Monitor for adverse drug reactions, and report medication errors and near misses immediately to the in-charge and through Datix. Store medicines safely (cold chain, expiry checks, separation of look-alike/sound-alike medicines), carry out the daily stock count, and request replenishment from the pharmacy to maintain minimum stock. Referral and transfer Identify newborns who meet referral criteria (e.g., need for mechanical ventilation, surgical conditions or care beyond SCANU capacity), as decided by the Neonatologist/SMO. Prepare the newborn for referral: pre-referral stabilisation (temperature, airway/oxygen, glucose, IV access), completed referral form with copies of investigations, and informed consent from the mother/caregiver. Coordinate with the referral focal point and ambulance team; accompany the newborn when assigned, maintaining thermal care and monitoring, and give a structured handover to the receiving facility. For internal transfers (labour room, OT, Emergency Department, maternity and SCANU), give verbal and written handover and complete the transfer log. Record each referral and its outcome in the referral register, and follow up feedback from the receiving facility. Infection prevention and control (IPC) Practise hand hygiene at the WHO 5 Moments, and aseptic technique for IV lines, feeds and procedures. Ensure incubators, radiant warmers, CPAP and phototherapy units are cleaned and disinfected on schedule, working with the hygiene team, and apply isolation or cohorting as per protocol. Dispose of sharps at the point of use, by the person who used them, into a sharps container kept within reach. Never recap needles or leave needles or cannula stylets aside. Report any sharps injury immediately for first aid and post-exposure assessment. Segregate clinical waste correctly, and follow hygiene standards for expressing and storing breast milk. Family-centred care and communication Inform mothers and caregivers daily about the newborn's condition, treatment and plan, in a language they understand (Bangla, Rohingya or Chittagonian), and obtain and document informed consent. Promote Kangaroo Mother Care, breastfeeding and mothers' participation in care. Provide discharge counselling on danger signs, feeding, thermal care, immunisation and follow-up, and document it. Provide compassionate support to families, including bereavement care, in line with MCH protocol. Documentation, handover and reporting Keep complete, accurate and timely clinical records and registers (admission, discharge, referral and death). Give a structured verbal and written handover at the bedside at every shift change. Submit the daily SCANU census and weekly medication consumption and activity reports on time, using MCH reporting formats. Maintain patient confidentiality in all records and communication. Infant security and quality (MCH-specific) The role holder will: Apply mother–baby ID bands and check them at every procedure, transfer and discharge; never leave a newborn unattended, and hand babies only to the verified mother/caregiver or authorised staff. Follow infant security procedures: controlled access to SCANU, visitor/attendant passes, transfer logs, head counts each shift, and participation in missing-baby (Code Pink) drills. Provide respectful, dignified and non-discriminatory care in line with the MCH Hospital Charter, admission/discharge criteria and visiting/attendant policies. Report clinical incidents, near misses and adverse events through Datix (or manual notification) within 24 hours, and take part in clinical audits, neonatal death reviews and quality improvement activities. Follow the SCI Bangladesh and MCH security plan (camp access, movement rules, curfew and ID card requirements), and SCI administrative procedures for attendance, roster, leave, shift exchange, timesheets and care of assets. Professional development Complete the SCANU competency checklist and mandatory trainings within the timeframes set out below, keep neonatal resuscitation skills up to date, and support the orientation and mentoring of new nurses and nursing students.

job_description: Job Description: OT incharge- Jointly operated by Save the Children & PHD Mother and Child Hospital (MCH). Duty Station: Camp 21, Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar Position Summary The OT In-Charge is responsible for the overall management, coordination, supervision, and effective operation of the Operation Theatre (OT) at the Mother and Child Hospital (MCH), Teknaf. The position holder will ensure the delivery of safe, quality, and evidence-based perioperative nursing care to patients undergoing obstetric, gynaecological, general surgical, and other surgical procedures within the hospital's approved service capacity. The OT In-Charge will oversee daily OT operations, supervise OT nurses and assigned support staff, ensure adequate staffing and duty roster management, maintain the availability and functionality of surgical instruments, equipment, and essential supplies, and ensure strict compliance with infection prevention and control (IPC), surgical safety, and patient care protocols. The position holder will work closely with surgeons, obstetricians, anaesthesia personnel, medical officers, nursing teams, CSSD, Pharmacy, Admin & Logistics, and other relevant departments to ensure smooth coordination and continuity of surgical services. The role will also contribute to clinical quality improvement, staff capacity building, performance monitoring, and compliance with PHD policies, applicable Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) standards, and humanitarian principles. Duty Station The primary duty station is the MCH Operation Theatre, Teknaf. The position holder may be required to coordinate with the recovery area, emergency department, labour room, maternity ward, and other relevant clinical departments to ensure effective delivery and continuity of surgical services. Key Responsibilities Overall OT Management and Operational Coordination Lead, organize, and supervise the overall daily operation of the Operation Theatre to ensure efficient, safe, and uninterrupted surgical services. Develop and implement appropriate OT operational plans, workflows, and procedures in coordination with MCH management. Coordinate daily and emergency surgical schedules with surgeons, obstetricians, anaesthesia personnel, medical officers, and relevant clinical departments. Ensure the OT is adequately prepared, equipped, clean, and functional before scheduled and emergency procedures. Monitor the readiness of the OT, recovery area, surgical instruments, equipment, sterile supplies, and emergency resources. Ensure appropriate coordination between the OT, labour room, emergency department, maternity ward, inpatient units, and CSSD. Monitor daily OT activities and ensure timely management of operational challenges and service interruptions. Ensure appropriate arrangements for emergency obstetric and surgical procedures, including emergency caesarean sections, according to hospital service capacity. Identify operational gaps and recommend appropriate corrective measures to MCH management. Ensure continuity of OT services during emergencies, staff shortages, and other operational challenges. Clinical Supervision and Quality of Patient Care Supervise and monitor the clinical performance of OT nurses and assigned staff to ensure quality and safe perioperative nursing care. Ensure appropriate pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative nursing care in accordance with approved clinical protocols. Ensure proper patient identification, verification of surgical procedures, surgical site confirmation, and consent documentation in coordination with the responsible clinical team. Ensure proper implementation and documentation of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist, including sign-in, time-out, and sign-out. Monitor compliance with aseptic techniques, sterile field maintenance, safe instrument handling, and surgical safety procedures. Ensure proper surgical instrument, needle, and swab counts in collaboration with the surgical team. Monitor patient safety during surgical procedures and ensure timely escalation of clinical concerns and complications. Ensure appropriate patient transfer, recovery monitoring, clinical observation, and structured handover. Review nursing documentation and ensure accuracy, completeness, and timely reporting. Identify gaps in clinical practice and provide necessary guidance, supervision, and corrective feedback to OT staff. Promote patient-centered care, dignity, confidentiality, and respectful treatment of all patients and caregivers. Staff Management, Supervision, and Duty Roster Supervise, guide, and provide technical support to OT nurses and other assigned OT personnel. Prepare, review, and manage the OT duty roster in accordance with hospital requirements and the approved 48-hour duty roster, as applicable. Ensure adequate staffing coverage for scheduled surgeries, emergency procedures, and shift operations. Monitor staff attendance, punctuality, performance, and adherence to assigned duties and responsibilities. Allocate daily responsibilities among OT staff according to their qualifications, competencies, and service requirements. Conduct regular staff briefings, shift handovers, and operational meetings to ensure effective communication and coordination. Identify staff training needs and facilitate orientation, coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job training. Assess staff performance and provide constructive feedback to improve clinical competency and professional development. Promote teamwork, professional conduct, accountability, and a supportive working environment. Report staff performance concerns, attendance irregularities, and disciplinary issues to the designated supervisor in accordance with organizational procedures.  Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) Ensure strict implementation of MCH IPC guidelines, standard precautions, and surgical asepsis procedures within the OT. Monitor compliance with WHO's Five Moments of Hand Hygiene and appropriate use of personal protective equipment (PPE). Ensure proper cleaning, disinfection, decontamination, sterilization, and storage of surgical instruments and reusable equipment. Coordinate with CSSD or the designated sterilization team to ensure the availability of sterile instruments and supplies. Ensure appropriate separation and handling of clean, sterile, contaminated, and used equipment. Monitor proper segregation, handling, and disposal of sharps, infectious waste, and other clinical waste. Conduct regular IPC monitoring and ensure timely corrective actions for identified gaps or breaches. Ensure immediate reporting and appropriate follow-up of sharps injuries, occupational exposures, and infection prevention incidents. Participate in IPC audits, training sessions, and quality improvement initiatives. Surgical Equipment, Instruments, and Supplies Management Oversee the management, maintenance, and accountability of all OT equipment, surgical instruments, consumables, and other resources. Ensure regular assessment of the functionality, cleanliness, completeness, and safety of surgical equipment and instruments. Monitor the availability of essential surgical supplies, sterile packs, sutures, dressings, PPE, and emergency consumables. Maintain an updated inventory of OT instruments, equipment, and consumables. Monitor stock levels, consumption patterns, and replenishment requirements to prevent stockouts and service interruptions. Ensure appropriate storage, handling, expiry monitoring, and authorized use of OT supplies. Report damaged, missing, expired, or malfunctioning equipment and instruments to the appropriate department. Coordinate with Admin & Logistics, Procurement & Supply Chain, Biomedical, Pharmacy, and CSSD teams regarding procurement, maintenance, repair, and replenishment requirements. Ensure proper documentation of equipment maintenance, instrument accountability, and stock utilization. Emergency Preparedness and Patient Safety Ensure the OT is prepared to respond to emergency obstetric and surgical procedures. Monitor the availability and readiness of emergency equipment, including oxygen, suction apparatus, resuscitation equipment, and other essential supplies. Ensure OT staff are familiar with emergency response procedures and their respective responsibilities. Coordinate with the clinical team during emergency procedures to facilitate timely and effective service delivery. Ensure immediate escalation of patient deterioration, excessive bleeding, suspected anaesthetic complications, and other critical incidents. Facilitate staff participation in emergency drills, resuscitation training, and patient safety activities. Ensure proper reporting and documentation of adverse events, near misses, medication errors, and other patient safety incidents. Review reported incidents and coordinate appropriate corrective and preventive actions with MCH management. Documentation, Reporting, and Data Management Ensure accurate and timely maintenance of OT registers, surgical records, patient care documentation, and other required clinical records. Monitor daily, weekly, and monthly OT service statistics, including surgical procedures, emergency procedures, and other relevant service indicators. Ensure accurate recording and reporting of OT activities in accordance with PHD and MCH reporting requirements. Review OT documentation for completeness, accuracy, and consistency. Prepare and submit regular OT activity reports, staffing updates, supply requirements, and operational challenges to the designated supervisor. Maintain proper documentation of duty rosters, staff attendance, equipment inventories, instrument counts, and stock utilization. Ensure confidentiality, security, and appropriate management of patient information and clinical records. Support clinical audits, data quality assessments, service monitoring, and quality improvement activities. Coordination, Communication, and Teamwork Maintain effective coordination with surgeons, obstetricians, anaesthesia personnel, medical officers, Nursing In-Charge, recovery nurses, and other relevant clinical teams. Ensure smooth communication and coordination between OT, labour room, emergency, maternity, inpatient services, and CSSD. Coordinate with hospital management and relevant departments to address operational, staffing, equipment, and supply-related challenges. Participate in clinical coordination meetings, departmental reviews, and hospital management meetings as required. Promote effective teamwork, mutual respect, professional communication, and accountability among OT personnel. Support integrated MCH operations and collaborate with other departments to ensure continuity and quality of patient care. Training, Capacity Building, and Quality Improvement Identify clinical and operational capacity gaps among OT staff and recommend appropriate training interventions. Organize and facilitate regular orientation, refresher training, and on-the-job coaching for OT nurses and assigned personnel. Provide practical guidance on surgical asepsis, instrument handling, patient safety, IPC, and emergency preparedness. Monitor the application of training outcomes and provide follow-up support to improve staff competency. Participate in clinical audits, quality improvement initiatives, and implementation of corrective actions. Promote evidence-based nursing practices and continuous improvement in OT service delivery. Safeguarding and Accountability The position holder must comply with PHD's Code of Conduct, Save the Children's safeguarding policies, Child Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) requirements, anti-harassment standards, and applicable organizational procedures. Ensure that all patients and caregivers are treated with dignity, respect, and without discrimination. Protect patient privacy and maintain confidentiality of medical and personal information. Ensure that staff under supervision comply with safeguarding standards and professional codes of conduct. Promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for patients, caregivers, and colleagues. Report safeguarding concerns, suspected abuse, exploitation, harassment, or serious misconduct through established reporting mechanisms. Ensure accountability for clinical supervision, staff management, and operational decisions within the assigned scope of responsibility. Follow established patient complaint, incident reporting, and accountability mechanisms. Maintain professional conduct, punctuality, confidentiality, and accountability. Follow the approved duty roster, shift handover procedures, attendance requirements, and hospital security protocols. Ensure proper utilization and protection of organizational assets, surgical equipment, supplies, and infrastructure. Participate in mandatory training, clinical reviews, and organizational meetings. Support emergency response activities and continuity of hospital services when required. Perform other relevant duties assigned by the supervisor that are consistent with the purpose of the position.

job_description: Job Context: Vacancy:  03 (Chilmari, Ramkrishnapur and Pragpur Union of Daulatpur Upazila under Khustia District). Job Summary: The position is for the "Digi-Gram: Democratizing Digital Public Services through Community-Led Action" project, Supported by British Council and Funded by  the European Union. The Social Mobilizer will play a critical role to Improve inclusive access of vulnerable women to digital public services, including Union Digital Center services, civil registration and certification, and Social Safety Net Programme (SSNP) services, with reduced barriers to online applications, documentation, approvals and service follow-up of Mother and Child Benefit Programme (MCBP) for community participation at the grassroots level. By acting as a bridge between the project team and local communities, the Social Mobilizer will ensure the effective implementation of project activities, facilitate meaningful engagement with community level stakeholders, and drive initiatives that benefit marginalized mother and pregnant women to take active roles in digital literacy, e-governance.  Working locations:  The position is based in union level in Daulatpur Upazila under Kushtia District. Candidate from Ulipur, Ramkrisnapur & Pragpur Union of Daulatpur Upazila under Khustia District will be get preference.  Duration:  Initially 9.5 months with possibility of extension based on performance and availability of fund. Reportable To:  Digital Inclusion Facilitator. He/she will collaborate closely with the project team Job Responsibilities Lead community-level mobilisation and outreach in the three targeted unions and Facilitate and implement project activities at the union level in coordination with local stakeholders. Identify and engage pregnant and potentially eligible women, families and vulnerable community members.  Organise community/courtyard awareness sessions and Gramer Digital Shobha sessions, support participant registration and follow-up, and maintain regular communication with local leaders and community groups.  Organize community meetings, workshops, and training sessions to promote digital literacy, digital public services, including Union Digital Center services, civil registration and certification, and Social Safety Net Programme (SSNP) services, with reduced barriers to online applications, documentation, approvals and service follow-up of Mother and Child Benefit Programme (MCBP). Collect community feedback and report emerging service-access barriers to the project team. Provide technical assistance to mother and pregnant women on Digital literacy through using mobile responsive web application. To increase community awareness and digital skills, while strengthening support through the engagement of husbands, family members, community leaders, and local influencers. To generate community-level evidence on digital service barriers and use it to promote more accessible, transparent, and inclusive Mother and Child Benefit Programme (MCBP) services. Engage with union parishad members, community leaders, and mother and pregnant women to foster e-governance practices. Assist in developing communication materials and awareness campaigns on gender equality. Ensure timely reporting and documentation of project activities and progress.
